author: Werth, Nicolas
title: Crimes and Mass Violence of the Russian Civil Wars (1918-1921)
publisher: Mass Violence and Resistance, Sciences Po, Paris
notes: An open-access encyclopedia entry by the historian who wrote the Soviet chapter of The Black Book of Communism, published in 2008 and drawing on the post-1991 archives. Read in full; it has no pagination, so it is cited by its section headings. It is the pack's source for the periodised figures it does give - the executions of September-October 1918, the Tambov camps, the pogrom total - and for the two framing claims it makes: that no side had a monopoly of violence, and that the Bolsheviks nonetheless theorised it as mass terror to a far greater degree than anyone else. Werth is one voice in a contested count and is cited as one.
